## d80d51ff509a

**Reproduced defect — exact controls are coercive and unknown axes are ignored.**
The audit source SHA-256
`a2387b78717a08ed6292efbb70bd08079aebba3ade8764a4908f6b77bdfd0d76`
matches the assignment. With the same seed/sample, baseline `grid_h=12,
grid_w=16`, string values `"12"/"16"`, fractional values `12.9/16.9`, and an
unknown `typo_axis=123` all return the same lawful 12×16 grid, SHA-256
`3ad65c41ccbd9418fdb3917de30dd32f5c76d05b32f5bff1c4a6abff0e56d044`.
The strings are coerced, fractions are truncated, and the typo is silently
ignored; `self_check` returns `[]` in every case.

Reproducer: `checks/audit/d80d51ff509a/reproduce.py`. Structured result:
`checks/audit/d80d51ff509a/finding.json`. The first invocation log records an
invalid private runtime alias; the corrected source-bound loader run is retained
in `reproduce-fixed.log`.

Suggested repair: validate literal integer call/axis values and unknown keys
before `gen_ctx`, then add focused tests for bool/string/integral-float/fractional
values and exact observability. Scope is source-contract only; I did not execute
or judge its Racket labels and did not modify the audited source.
